reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch deny a double rejection, reading 1 Samuel 13 as only forfeiting the dynasty's future, with Saul's own personal rejection placed in chapter 15's later offense.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen reads chapter 13's rupture over the sacrifice as a separate, earlier composite narrative rivaling chapter 15's Agag rejection account.

quotes.text: Comparing with this original the copy in xiii. 7-15, we are struck, in the first place, with the placing of the rupture so much earlier. Scarcely is Saul made king when he is deposed, on the spot, at Gilgal.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on 1 Samuel 13:14.

sides.snippet: But now your kingdom shall not continue: Yahweh has sought him a man after his own heart
sides.verseText: But now your kingdom shall not continue: Yahweh has sought him a man after his own heart, and Yahweh has appointed him to be prince over his people, because you have not kept that which Yahweh commanded you.

sides.snippet: It repents me that I have set up Saul to be king; for he is turned back from following me
sides.verseText: It repents me that I have set up Saul to be king; for he is turned back from following me, and has not performed my commandments. Samuel was angry; and he cried to Yahweh all night.
